title: Response to Leader's Statement on 6 March 2018
what_it_is: Response to Leader's Statement on 6 March 2018

sections.label: Statement on exchanges with Ministers
sections.summary: The speaker says he wrote to the Speaker on 5 March to state he wished to make a statement on his exchanges with Ministers Heng Swee Keat and Shanmugam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Pursuant to the resolution passed by the House on Tuesday, 6 March, I wish to make my Statement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I had written to Speaker on Monday evening, 5 March, to inform him that I wish to make a statement in the House concerning the exchanges I had with Ministers Heng Swee Keat and Shanmugam during the Budget Round-up on 1 March.

sections.label: PM Lee on raising taxes
sections.summary: At the 2017 PAP Convention, Prime Minister Lee said the Government would raise taxes as spending grew, and that Finance Minister Heng was right that it was a matter of when.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In November 2017, during the People's Action Party (PAP) Convention, Prime Minister Lee announced definitively that the Government would be raising taxes as Government spending on investments and social services grew.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He further stated that Finance Minister Heng was right when he said raising taxes was not a matter of whether but when.

sections.label: No pre-2021 GST commitment
sections.summary: The Government did not publicly commit before Budget 2018 that it would not raise GST before 2021; this was announced on 19 February 2018 in the Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is notable is that nowhere in the discussions just before Budget 2018 did the Government publicly commit that it would not raise GST before 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This was only announced on 19 February 2018 during the Budget Statement.

sections.label: Notice over dishonourable conduct
sections.summary: The Member is put on notice, and the House too, that repeating such dishonourable conduct and abuse of Parliamentary Privilege would be referred to the Committee of Privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: By so refusing, her conduct falls short of the standard of integrity and honour expected of all Members.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: I must, therefore, put the hon Member on notice and the rest of the House, too, that if she repeats such dishonourable conduct and abuse Parliamentary Privilege, I would refer the matter to the Committee of Privileges.

sections.label: No retraction or apology
sections.summary: The speaker says he sees no reason to retract his statements, will not apologise, and was doing his duty as an MP to let the Government account to the people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And this also is the standard that the Prime Minister has said earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I do not see any reason for me to retract the statements which I made during the exchanges with the Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my earlier statement, there was a sequence of events which led me to have that suspicion, contributed to by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: And secondly, Sir, I will not apologise to this House because I believe that I was doing my duty as an MP in the Constitutional role that we have been elected into, to give the Government the forum to account to the people.

sections.label: Interpretation of Ms Lim's statement
sections.summary: The speaker says Ms Lim meant the Government would have raised GST immediately if not for adverse public reaction and its earlier statement that it had enough money for the decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Otherwise, if the announcement had not been made, perhaps we would be debating a GST hike today." I think what Ms Lim meant by that statement is that she was suggesting that the Government would have raised GST immediately, if not for that adverse public reaction when it "floated" the suggestion late last year and if it had not "stuck" with the previous statement that it had enough money for the decade.

sections.label: Withdrawal of statement request
sections.summary: A member asks another to withdraw a statement after facts and clarifications were made available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Parliament is a serious forum for us to discuss serious matters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Now that you have the opportunity to gather all the facts, now that I and my colleagues have made all the clarifications, and you had the chance over the last few days since you made the statement to check the Hansard, to check whatever facts, I think it is only right and honourable that you withdraw the statement.

sections.label: GST intention and possible error
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government refuted intending to raise GST this year and accepts possibly being wrong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: And as I said in my speech earlier, the Government has said it has refuted that they had any intention to raise the GST this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I do not know the truth so I can accept that I may have been wrong.

sections.label: Basis for belief questioned
sections.summary: The speaker asks Ms Lim whether she has a basis for her belief and accepts the explanations given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But now, having had so many days to examine the facts, I would like to know whether Ms Lim, do you have a basis for your belief?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And now, do you accept the explanations that have been given that this has been the intention of the Government, there was no back-tracking, that this was the fact as we had put out?

sections.label: Suspicion basis and MP duty
sections.summary: The speaker says discussing details and timing before a Budget is improper and rejects having no basis or failing duty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And I do not think it is proper for us to talk about the details and timing of it, way in advance of a Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I have said in my speech earlier that I can accept that my suspicion may have been wrong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But I do not accept that my suspicion had no basis and I do not accept that I had failed or been derelict in my duty as an MP to this House.
